questions.q: What does Siddhartha conclude about the material and spiritual worlds?
a: Neither one is complete without the other
The spiritual world should replace the material one
The material world is the only true reality
Both worlds should be avoided entirely
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he rejects both extremes and looks for balance.

questions.q: What happens when Siddhartha lives only as an ascetic?
a: He finds the path incomplete without the physical world
He reaches enlightenment straight away
He becomes wealthy and content
He forgets his friend Govinda
questions.why: Lesson 1 says asceticism alone left him unfulfilled.

questions.q: What does the fisherman represent in the summary?
a: The enlightenment and freedom Siddhartha seeks
The dangers of a selfish life
The wisdom of city merchants
The strict rules of the Buddha
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls the fisherman the symbol of Siddhartha's goal.

a: The interconnection of all things
The power of unfulfilled desire
The passage from youth to age
The emptiness of the natural world
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses the river to show everything flowing together.

questions.q: What causes suffering, according to Siddhartha and Govinda?
a: Desire and attachment to things we lack
Too much contact with other people
A lack of money and comfortable shelter
Disobeying religious teachers
questions.why: The overview says desire for what we lack creates suffering.
